localChanges: A Wonder lost when its city is destroyed can never be built again, by anyone, as in the original. Before, it could be built a second time (closes #971).

Nuclear units can still be built after the Manhattan Project is lost, and spaceship parts after the Apollo Program is lost. A civilization that comes into the game afterwards still gets a spaceship (#971).
In a game saved before this, a city building a lost Wonder again stops at its next turn and keeps its shields (#971).

log: Spaceship parts stay buildable after the Apollo Program is lost with its city, and a civilization that arrives afterwards still gets a ship: v474.05 asks whether the Apollo Program was ever built, not whether it still stands (civ-clone/web-renderer#971).

A Wonder lost when its city is destroyed has still been built: nobody can build it again, and Nuclear units stay buildable after the Manhattan Project is lost, as in v474.05, where a lost Wonder is marked lost, not un-built (civ-clone/web-renderer#971). Before, a lost Wonder could be built again and no new Nuclear unit could be chosen.
A game saved earlier with a lost Wonder part-way through being built again has that build dropped at its next turn, with its shields kept.

`lib/wonderHistory` gives the one answer the rules and reports read: `everBuilt`, `wonderStatus` (standing, lost or never; where; whose) and `wonderHistory`, in the original's order. Effects, score and the Great Library still read the Wonder standing, and whose it is.

The registry of city improvements can be asked for every improvement of a type with `getByType(Type, includeDestroyed)`, by exact class, kept in an index so the question is cheap inside a city's build choices. `getByCity`'s `includeDestroyed` now does what it says: it was ignored, and nothing passed it (civ-clone/web-renderer#971).
Nothing changes for a game until a ruleset asks.
